subject.title: chore(deps): bump the actions group across 1 directory with 14 updates

question: Should OpenClaw approve the updated immutable revisions of `openai/codex-action` and the other secret-bearing GitHub Actions for workflows that pass private keys, registry credentials, release privileges, or OpenAI API keys?
rationale: The repository policy requires direct dependency inspection for dependency-backed behavior and a personal Codex-source check for Codex-related verdicts; this is a trust decision over third-party executable workflow code, not a mechanical code repair.

options.title: Audit and approve revisions
options.body: Review the upstream commits and action behavior for every credential-bearing call site, then permit the updated pins after exact-head workflow evidence is available.

options.title: Split sensitive upgrades
options.body: Land only action revisions that do not execute with sensitive credentials and defer the secret-bearing revisions for a dedicated security review.

options.title: Hold this Dependabot rollup
options.body: Close or pause this rollup and regenerate narrow dependency updates after the action trust policy is confirmed.

recommendation.title: Audit and approve revisions
recommendation.body: Review the upstream commits and action behavior for every credential-bearing call site, then permit the updated pins after exact-head workflow evidence is available.

likelyOwner.reason: Likely repository-level workflow and release routing owner, though direct file-history attribution could not be completed in this read-only environment.
